7. Terracotta figurine

Terracotta figurine, MU2676, front view © Gale History Museum

Humanoid clay figurine of beige colour. Modelling at the top of the head may represent either a short hairstyle or a headdress. The face is shaped with a long, pointed nose. Holes in the clay indicate eyes and a mouth. There is no indication of a chin; the head and neck seamlessly merge. The body is very loosely moulded, with the indication of arms and hands held inwards and against the body, made from pinched and folded clay. The lower body flares widely to an amorphous fluted shape. The object rests on a small black (modern) square plinth, held in place by short metal prongs on either side of the figurine base.
